brief: The canvas displays the memory of architecture in a state of slow decay. Warm, golden shapes—walls and arches—are constructed of solidified beeswax, appearing dense and luminous. Over time, these defined forms soften, losing their edges, and collapse into a viscous, honey-colored resin pool. The movement is overwhelmingly slow and gravitational, showing the viscous material flowing and pooling across the surface. The colors shift from pale amber to deep gold as the material settles into a continuous, amorphous puddle. The viewer observes the entropy of the structure, watching discrete memories yield to liquid form.

statement: This sketch visualizes the slow decay of architectural memory through the transformation of solid beeswax forms into a viscous honey pool. Initially, warm golden rectangles represent defined structures that gradually shrink and lose their edges, becoming fluid amorphous blobs. The simulation captures the entropic process where discrete architectural elements dissolve into continuous liquid form, with colors shifting from pale amber to deep gold as they settle. The viewer observes an ever-flowing landscape of memory yielding to time's gravitational pull, rendered through thousands of particles that morph seamlessly from solid geometry to liquid pools.
